title_en: China Nonferrous Metals Industry Changsha Survey and Design Research Institute v. Hainan Huifu Real Estate Development Company Changsha Branch and Hainan Huifu Real Estate Development Company — dispute over cooperative building construction contract

full_text_en:
China Nonferrous Metal Industry Changsha Survey and Design Research Institute v. Hainan Huifu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Changsha Branch and Hainan Huifu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over cooperative building contract

Ruling Summary

The basis for retrying a case in accordance with the trial supervision procedure is that the legally effective judgment or ruling is indeed erroneous, or that there is evidence proving that the legally effective mediation agreement violates the principle of voluntary mediation or that the content of the mediation agreement is illegal. Correcting errors in the original trial is the basic function of retrial. Therefore, a retrial should be conducted within the scope of the original trial, and judgment should not be rendered beyond that scope.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2006) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 28

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Nonferrous Metal Industry Changsha Survey and Design Research Institute, domiciled at No. 81 Shaoshan North Road, Changsha City, Hunan Province.
Legal Representative: Yang Chuande, President of the Institute.
Agent ad litem: Jin Yiyuan, Vice President of the Institute.
Agent ad litem: Yang Wanlin, lawyer of Beijing Chang'an Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Hainan Huifu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Changsha Branch, domiciled at Room 1, 4th Door, Building 15, Block 2, Hongqi District, Changsha City, Hunan Province.
Person in Charge: Fu Xiaohua, Manager of the Branch.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Hainan Huifu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at 3rd Floor, Building 5, Dianhua New Village, Haikou City, Hainan Province.
Legal Representative: Tang Yuguang, General Manager of the Company.

Respondent (Third Party at First Instance): Hunan Xiongxin Construction Co., Ltd., domiciled at Shijiapo, Kaifu District, Changsha City, Hunan Province.
Legal Representative: Zhou Qifei, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Che Ning, male, born on October 12, 1970, native of Changsha City, Hunan Province, residing at Room 602, Building 2, No. 226 Laodong West Road, Tianxin District, Changsha City, Hunan Province.
Agent ad litem: Gong Ziping, lawyer of Hunan Guangji Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over a cooperative building contract between the plaintiff at first instance China Nonferrous Metal Industry Changsha Survey and Design Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as Changsha Survey Institute) and the defendants at first instance Hainan Huifu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Changsha Branch (hereinafter referred to as Huifu Changsha Company) and Hainan Huifu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huifu Company), the Hunan High People's Court rendered a Civil Mediation Document (1997) Xiang Min Chu Zi No. 7 on March 19, 1998, which has become legally effective. An outsider, China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Changsha Office (hereinafter referred to as Orient Asset Changsha Office), raised an objection. The Hunan High People's Court issued a Civil Ruling (2004) Xiang Gao Fa Min Jian Zi No. 148 on September 8, 2004, deciding to retry the case. During this period, Hunan Xiongxin Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xiongxin Company) took over the creditor's rights of Orient Asset Changsha Office and applied to participate in the proceedings. The Hunan High People's Lawfully formed a new collegial panel, added Xiongxin Company as a third party in the case, and rendered a Civil Judgment (2004) Xiang Gao Fa Min Zai Zi No. 148 on February 21, 2006. The appellant, Changsha Survey Institute, refused to accept this judgment and appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on July 6, 2006. Jin Yiyuan and Yang Wanlin, agents ad litem of Changsha Survey Institute, and Che Ning and Gong Ziping, agents ad litem of Xiongxin Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Huifu Changsha Company and Huifu Company, after being summoned by subpoena of this Court, did not appear in court. This case is now concluded.

The retrial by the Hunan High People's Court found the following facts: On November 25, 1994, Changsha Survey Institute and Huifu Changsha Company signed a "Cooperative Building Contract" stipulating that Changsha Survey Institute would use its right to use 7.928 mu of land located at No. 81 Shaoshan North Road, Changsha City, obtained by administrative allocation, as an investment to build a cooperative building with Huifu Changsha Company. On December 16 of the same year, Changsha Survey Institute signed a land use right transfer contract with the land administration department and paid the land transfer fee as required. At the same time, at the request of Huifu Changsha Company, Changsha Survey Institute applied to transfer the land use right to the name of Huifu Changsha Company. After review, the land administration department handled the red-line map and transfer procedures for the land, and issued a state-owned land use right certificate for the land to Huifu Changsha Company. On December 28, 1994, Changsha Survey Institute and Huifu Changsha Company formally signed a "Contract for Cooperative Construction of 'Jin Fu Mansion'" stipulating that Changsha Survey Institute would provide the construction land, and Huifu Changsha Company would bear all construction-related funds, and the distribution of the constructed buildings, liability for breach of contract, and other matters were agreed upon. After the contract was signed, Changsha Survey Institute carried out work such as housing demolition and relocation on the construction land as agreed, while Huifu Changsha Company invested part of the construction funds and commenced work on demolition compensation, preliminary project approval, construction application, organization of survey and design, and part of the basic foundation works and water and electricity capacity increase. During the cooperation, Huifu Changsha Company separately rented part of Changsha Survey Institute's office space, and still owed part of the rent and utilities to Changsha Survey Institute. Subsequently, due to the inability of Huifu Changsha Company to provide follow-up construction funds, the joint construction project was suspended in July 1996. The parties failed to reach a resolution after multiple negotiations. Changsha Survey Institute filed a lawsuit with the Changsha Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province on August 4, 1997. Huifu Changsha Company raised a jurisdictional objection, and the Hunan High People's Court took over the case for trial. After mediation presided over by the original trial of the Hunan High People's Court, the parties voluntarily reached the following agreement on March 19, 1998: 1. Due to reasons such as Huifu Changsha Company's lack of proper subject qualification, the cooperative building contract, the land use right transfer agreement, and related contracts (agreements) signed between it and Changsha Survey Institute were all invalid, and Huifu Changsha Company unconditionally returned to Changsha Survey Institute the land use right of 7.928 mu at No. 81 Shaoshan Road, and transferred all relevant materials related to the cooperative project to Changsha Survey Institute. 2. The existing foundation pit project of the joint construction project on that land was transferred to Changsha Survey Institute. Before this mediation agreement, Huifu Changsha Company's debts under the project (including foundation pit earthwork, civil engineering, design payments, etc.) were all borne by Huifu Changsha Company. 3. The air conditioners, desks, and other office furniture in the office space currently rented by Huifu Changsha Company from Changsha Survey Institute were all offset against part of the rent and utilities it owed to Changsha Survey Institute. In addition, Huifu Changsha Company separately compensated Changsha Survey Institute for economic losses of RMB 3,000,000. 4. The case acceptance fee of RMB 122,910 and the property preservation fee of RMB 100,000 were borne by Huifu Changsha Company. 5. Huifu Company assumed joint and several liability for Huifu Changsha Company's obligations under the above agreement. After the mediation document was signed and received by both parties and became legally effective, Changsha Survey Institute applied for enforcement, and the land was transferred from Huifu Changsha Company to Changsha Survey Institute in September 1998. Changsha Survey Institute developed the land, built commercial housing for sale, and the land use rights have been allocated to the names of individual households.

The retrial by the Hunan High People's Court also found the following facts: In March 1995, during the construction of the "Jin Fu Mansion" project, Huifu Changsha Company used the land of the "Jin Fu Mansion" project as security for two "Loan Contracts" under which Changsha High-tech Development Zone Jinhai Co., Ltd., Haikou Company, Changsha Branch (hereinafter referred to as Jinhai Changsha Company) borrowed RMB 3,000,000 and RMB 1,000,000 from the Changsha Branch of Bank of China, and completed the mortgage registration procedures. Because Jinhai Changsha Company failed to repay the loans, the Changsha Branch of Bank of China filed a lawsuit with the Tianxin District People's Court of Changsha, Hunan Province. On December 22, 1997, the court rendered civil judgments (1997) Tian Jing Chu Zi No. 354 and No. 367 on the two loan contract disputes, respectively, holding that the mortgages were valid, ordering Jinhai Changsha Company to repay the principal of RMB 4,000,000 and interest, with Changsha High-tech Development Zone Jinhai Co., Ltd., Haikou Company bearing joint and several liability for repayment; and Huifu Changsha Company bearing joint and several liability within the scope of the mortgage guarantee. None of the parties appealed, and the judgments became legally effective. In June 2000, the creditor's rights were transferred from the Changsha Branch of Bank of China to Orient Asset Changsha Office. As of March 31, 2000, the principal of the creditor's rights was RMB 4,000,000, and the interest was RMB 1,964,290.36. In December 2004, Orient Asset Changsha Office transferred these creditor's rights to Xiongxin Company by public auction. Xiongxin Company provided the auction transaction confirmation, payment receipt for the auction price, and a list of principal and interest, indicating that it paid an auction commission of RMB 108,000 and purchased creditor's rights of RMB 8,901,509.5 at a transaction price of RMB 3,600,000.

The retrial by the Hunan High People's Court also found the following facts: Huifu Company was established in early 1993, with the competent authority being the Hainan Provincial Committee of the Chinese Revolutionary Committee of the Kuomintang, registered capital of RMB 20,000,000, and legal representative Tang Anyun. In May 1997, the company changed its legal representative to Tang Yuguang, Tang Anyun's younger brother. In November 2003, Huifu Company's business license was revoked by the Hainan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce for failure to undergo annual inspection. Huifu Changsha Company was established by Huifu Company, its registered capital of RMB 5,000,000 was not paid in full, the person in charge was Tang Anyun, later changed to Fu Xiaohua. In August 2001, Huifu Changsha Company's business license was revoked by the Changsha Administration for Industry and Commerce. The persons in charge of the above two companies are currently whereabouts unknown due to suspected fraud crimes.

Orient Asset Changsha Office raised an objection to the Hunan High People's Court, stating: 1. The disputed land had been mortgaged to the objector, and the objector had the right to priority compensation. The outcome of this case has a legal interest relationship with the objector, and the court should notify the objector to participate in the proceedings; 2. The handling of the land in the mediation document harmed the interests of the objector.

After taking over the creditor's rights of Orient Asset Changsha Office, Xiongxin Company requested the Hunan High People's Court: 1. To participate in the proceedings of this case as a third party; 2. To order Changsha Survey Institute to compensate for the loss of RMB 8,901,509.5 due to the inability to realize the mortgage.

The Hunan High People's Court held in the retrial that Changsha Survey Institute and Huifu Changsha Company reached a mediation agreement in the original trial, whereby Huifu Changsha Company returned the land use right of 7.928 mu at No. 81 Shaoshan Road to Changsha Survey Institute as agreed. However, before the mediation for return, Huifu Changsha Company had already used the land as security for Jinhai Changsha Company's debts, and the mortgage had been confirmed valid by the Tianxin District People's Court of Changsha, Hunan Province in civil judgments (1997) Tian Jing Chu Zi No. 354 and No. 367. Xiongxin Company has now taken over the creditor's rights against Jinhai Changsha Company and claims the mortgage right over the land in this case. Since the mortgage right is a right attached to the property and transfers with the transfer of the mortgaged property, the mortgagee may exercise the right of priority compensation on the mortgaged property. The land accepted by Changsha Survey Institute from Huifu Changsha Company had already been encumbered with the mortgage set by Huifu Changsha Company, and the validity of the mortgage is not affected by the transfer of the mortgaged property. Therefore, Xiongxin Company's exercise of the right of pursuit against Changsha Survey Institute complies with legal provisions and should be supported. Since Changsha Survey Institute has developed the land, built commercial housing for sale, and the land use rights have been allocated to the names of individual households, it is no longer realistic to sell the land. Changsha Survey Institute should legally bear the obligation to discharge all mortgage debts on behalf of the debtor, so that Huifu Changsha Company's mortgage debts are performed in accordance with the law, and after discharging the mortgage debts, Changsha Survey Institute has the right to seek recourse from Huifu Changsha Company. At the same time, the mediation agreement reached between Changsha Survey Institute, Huifu Changsha Company, and Huifu Company regarding their cooperative building contract dispute was the true expression of the parties' intent, and its content complies with legal provisions, so it is confirmed by this court. However, because the mediation document did not address the mortgage creditor's rights involved in the land returned by Huifu Changsha Company to Changsha Survey Institute, while confirming the mediation agreement for the return of the land in accordance with the law, the mortgage creditor's rights on the land should also be addressed in order to fairly protect the legitimate rights and interests of all parties concerned with the land in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 89(2) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 112 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), and Articles 180 and 130 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, after discussion and decision by the Judicial Committee of the Hunan High People's Court, the judgment was rendered as follows: (1) The Civil Mediation Document (1997) Xiang Min Chu Zi No. 7 of the Hunan High People's Court was affirmed; (2) Changsha Survey Institute was ordered to assume the liability for discharging the mortgage creditor's rights of Xiongxin Company on behalf of Huifu Changsha Company. After discharging the mortgage debts, Changsha Survey Institute may seek recourse from Huifu Company and Huifu Changsha Company in accordance with the law.

The appellant, Changsha Survey Institute, refused to accept the judgment of the first instance and appealed to this Court, stating: 1. The transfer of the land use right in this case was itself not lawful, and its recovery of the land use right was conducted in accordance with the law; 2. The judgment of the first instance was internally contradictory. Since the original mediation document was affirmed, it should not bear liability for compensation to a third party, and the second item of the judgment of the first instance was uncertain, unspecific, and unenforceable. Therefore, it requested the revocation of the second item of the judgment of the first instance. Before the hearing of this Court, Changsha Survey Institute submitted an application to add parties and a supplementary appeal brief, applying to add the Hainan Provincial Committee of the Chinese Revolutionary Committee of the Kuomintang, the Hainan Branch of China Construction Bank, Hainan Congxin Accounting Firm, and Hunan Gaoxin Industrial Co., Ltd. as third parties in this case, and requested a judgment to deny the corporate personality of Huifu Company, Huifu Changsha Company, and Changsha High-tech Development Zone Jinhai Co., Ltd., Haikou Company, and to order the Hainan Provincial Committee of the Chinese Revolutionary Committee of the Kuomintang to discharge the debts of Huifu Company and Huifu Changsha Company, and the Hainan Branch of China Construction Bank, Hainan Congxin Accounting Firm, and Hunan Gaoxin Industrial Co., Ltd. to bear joint and several liability for the debts of Huifu Company and Huifu Changsha Company. During the trial, Changsha Survey Institute also submitted that this case was a case subject to the trial supervision procedure, and the original trial did not involve the content of the land use right mortgage; adding Xiongxin Company as a third party in the retrial was improper; there was no direct legal relationship between it and Xiongxin Company, and Xiongxin Company was not a third party with an independent claim, so it should not be liable to Xiongxin Company. The respondent, Xiongxin Company, argued in defense: 1. A lawful mortgage had been established on the land use right in this case and confirmed by an effective judgment of the Tianxin District People's Court of Changsha, Hunan Province; after accepting the land use right, Changsha Survey Institute should bear the guarantee liability for the mortgage on the land use right in accordance with the law; 2. The judgment of the first instance was clear, specific, and without contradiction; 3. No party was omitted in the first instance; the application to add parties and the corresponding litigation claims raised by Changsha Survey Institute were not within the scope of trial of this case. In response to the claims raised by Changsha Survey Institute during the trial, Xiongxin Company argued that the reason for the retrial of this case was that the mediation document of the original trial infringed upon the interests of Xiongxin Company as the mortgagee; it was not improper for Xiongxin Company to join the retrial; the provision in the mediation document of the original trial regarding the transfer of the mortgaged property directly infringed upon the rights of the mortgagee; the transfer of the land use right cannot impede the rights of the mortgagee, so the judgment of the first instance, ordering Changsha Survey Institute to bear liability to Xiongxin Company, was correct.

The facts found by this Court in the second instance are the same as those found by the court of first instance.

This Court holds: The first instance proceeding in this case was initiated by the Hunan High People's Court based on the trial supervision procedure. Therefore, the scope of trial in this case should be limited by the scope of trial in the original trial. Before the mediation agreement of the original trial was reached, the mortgage rights taken over by Xiongxin Company had already been confirmed by the effective civil judgments (1997) Tian Jing Chu Zi No. 354 and No. 367 of the Tianxin District People's Court of Changsha, Hunan Province. Based on the right of pursuit inherent in a mortgage, the mortgagee may seek recourse against the ultimate transferee of the mortgaged property. Therefore, this mortgage right had already obtained a legal basis that could be realized in the enforcement proceedings. In the original trial, the dispute over the cooperative building contract between Changsha Survey Institute, Huifu Company, and Huifu Changsha Company did not involve the content of the land mortgage. Therefore, by addressing the mortgage right while affirming the mediation agreement of the original trial, the judgment of the first instance exceeded the scope of trial of the original trial.

Since Xiongxin Company participated in the proceedings upon its own application and was notified by the court of first instance, its litigation status, pursuant to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, is that of a third party without independent claims. The judgment of the first instance, ordering the plaintiff at first instance, Changsha Survey Institute, to bear liability to Xiongxin Company, a third party without independent claims, violated the principle of "no trial without complaint" in civil procedure.

As for the claims raised by Changsha Survey Institute during the second instance, namely "applying to add the Hainan Provincial Committee of the Chinese Revolutionary Committee of the Kuomintang and others as third parties, requesting a judgment to deny the corporate personality of Huifu Company, Huifu Changsha Company, and Changsha High-tech Development Zone Jinhai Co., Ltd., Haikou Company, and to order the Hainan Provincial Committee of the Chinese Revolutionary Committee of the Kuomintang to discharge the debts of Huifu Company and Huifu Changsha Company, and the Hainan Branch of China Construction Bank, Hainan Congxin Accounting Firm, and Hunan Gaoxin Industrial Co., Ltd. to bear joint and several liability for the debts of Huifu Company and Huifu Changsha Company," these also exceed the scope of trial of this case.

In summary, the original mediation document in this case has been in effect for several years and is not actually erroneous; it should be affirmed. The judgment of the retrial applied the law incorrectly and should be reversed. Pursuant to Article 153(1)(b) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment (2004) Xiang Gao Fa Min Zai Zi No. 148 of the Hunan High People's Court is reversed;
2. The Civil Mediation Document (1997) Xiang Min Chu Zi No. 7 of the Hunan High People's Court is affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 122,910 is to be borne by Hunan Xiongxin Construction Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Zhang Jinxian
Judge: Wu Xiaofang
Acting Judge: Song Chunyu

August 21, 2006

Clerk: Wei Da

Profile of the Presiding Judge

Zhang Jinxian, senior judge: born in 1955, Doctor of Laws. Appointed as a judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2000.
